jobContent:
■仕事概要
In short
You'll design and build Recho's inference framework for speech models and LLMs, and you'll own its throughput and GPU cost. This is a hands-on senior role: you'll architect the system and write much of the code yourself.
Team language:
English (Japanese not required)
Salary:
¥10M–¥20M per year, plus stock options
Location:
Tokyo (Hanzomon), hybrid. Candidates based outside Japan are welcome. We offer visa sponsorship and relocation support, and we're open to discussing fully remote arrangements.
You might be a fit if you are…
An MLOps
ML platform engineer who has built and tuned LLM inference stacks (vLLM, SGLang, etc.)
A speech recognition or speech synthesis engineer/researcher who wants to shift toward inference systems
An engineer who has optimized throughput and cost for inference workloads on large GPU clusters
About the role
At Recho, we run training, evaluation, data generation and large-scale batch inference across multiple speech models and LLMs. Your core mission is to independently design and implement a high-efficiency inference framework that serves all of them.
This isn't about wrapping a model in an API or tweaking config files. You'll need to understand each model's architecture, inputs and outputs, sequence lengths, pre- and post-processing, and GPU characteristics. From there, you'll separate and integrate model execution, batching, data processing and scheduling into a reusable inference architecture.
On the LLM side, you'll build on mature engines such as vLLM and SGLang. You'll tune model adaptation, inference parameters, batching, prefill/decode behavior and request priority. Across both speech and LLMs, your north star is throughput and GPU cost.
What this role is
not
Not an on-call or SRE role. SLA management, incident response and infrastructure maintenance for online services are not the focus.
GPU cluster operations and general DevOps are handled by a separate team.
Writing CUDA kernels or building an inference engine from scratch is not the main job.
RL training infrastructure belongs to our separate RL Infrastructure Engineer role. You'll partner with that team on the inference side.
What you'll do
1. Build a common inference framework for speech models
Design a shared inference architecture for ASR, TTS, speech-to-speech and other audio generation models
Draw clear boundaries between shared and model-specific modules, with adapter/plugin interfaces for onboarding new models
Build the inference APIs, SDKs and tooling our model teams use every day
2. Optimize large-scale batch inference for audio
Apply dynamic batching and bucketing for variable-length audio, and run data-parallel inference across GPUs and nodes
Build asynchronous pipelines that overlap preprocessing, inference, postprocessing and storage I/O
Measure and remove bottlenecks based on end-to-end processing time and cost
3. Adapt and optimize LLM inference
Stand up LLM inference on mature engines such as vLLM and SGLang
Tune tensor/pipeline parallelism, continuous batching, KV cache and prefix cache
Design scheduling that accounts for prefill/decode characteristics and task priority
4. Plan GPU usage for inference workloads
Handle GPU allocation and capacity planning for batch inference and evaluation
Orchestrate GPU inference jobs with Kubernetes, Slurm and Ray
Track and reduce GPU usage and inference cost per model and per task
We're happy to go into more detail during the intro call and interviews.
Why this role
Set the playbook in an area that doesn't have one yet.
Inference for variable-length audio, codecs, vocoders, speech-to-speech and multimodal models has no established best practices. What you design becomes the foundation for every future model and team.
Own inference end to end.
You'll cover both speech and LLMs, from framework design to batch inference and scheduling. That means you optimize the whole system, not just one piece of it.
Directly move the business.
Inference efficiency determines GPU cost per unit of generated speech and response latency. Those decide how competitive our product is for the major enterprises running it in production.
Tech stack
Languages & frameworks:
Python, PyTorch
LLM inference:
vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server
Speech models:
ASR, TTS, speech-to-speech, audio codecs, vocoders
Orchestration:
Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray
Low-level optimization (nice to have):
C++, CUDA, Triton, NCCL
Our product
We build the Recho AI Voice Platform, which delivers voice conversations natural enough to be hard to tell apart from a human. We also deploy and operate Voice AI Agents for large enterprises.
Our edge is a platform for building and improving high-quality agents quickly. It captures industry know-how and turns user feedback into a fast, continuous improvement loop. Our agents now handle complex, large-scale contact center operations in finance, manufacturing and the public sector. In some deployments, they've resolved every call without handing off to a human agent.
Hiring process
Intro call → Case assignment & first interview → Paid work trial* → Final interview → Offer meeting
*The work trial is 1–2 consecutive days at our Tokyo office, working on real tasks alongside the team, and it's paid. It's a chance for both sides to check fit and get a feel for the work.
If you're based outside Japan,
we'll agree on the format together. We won't ask you to travel to Japan just for this step.
If your schedule or your current employer's side-work policy makes the trial difficult, just let us know.
We may also ask for references.
About Recho
Recho develops foundation models for customer-support AI agents and also deploys them for clients, all within one organization. Our core strength is voice AI technology we built entirely in-house, which resolves the industry's long-standing trade-off between quality and cost.
We've closed a Series A of approximately ¥700M and are rapidly rolling out to demanding production environments at major companies such as SBI Shinsei Bank and KDDI.
